title: Comparing tuple sets in the labelled tree reduces to comparing the tuples coordinatewise
source_title: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings

standard_prerequisites.name: Back-and-forth relations on the labelled tree
standard_prerequisites.statement: The relations <=_alpha on tuples of the labelled tree are the usual back-and-forth relations of rank alpha, and they are monotone.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the relation being characterised.

standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphic downward closed subsets of the tree
standard_prerequisites.statement: S and T are finite downward closed subsets of the labelled tree, enumerated in an isomorphism.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two sides compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: Infinitely replicated branches
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every node of the labelled tree has infinitely many copies of its branch above it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes the upper cones of a node and of its class isomorphic.

core_obligations: The forward direction is monotonicity of the back-and-forth relations (source lines 517-518).

For the converse, observe that the upper cone of a node is definable from the node by restricting all quantifiers to be above it, so the cones inherit the coordinatewise comparison (source lines 520-525).
Partition the tree into the regions lying above exactly one enumeration point and use the infinite replication of branches to replace the cones by those disjoint regions (source lines 527-533).

Argue by contradiction with the back-and-forth game: a single losing position for S against T refines into components inside each region, where the existential player answers componentwise and wins on all regions, contradicting the assumption (source lines 535-543).

proof_roadmap.step: Transfer the comparison to the upper cones of the enumeration points.
Partition the tree by the regions above exactly one point and use branch replication.
Contradiction through a componentwise winning strategy in the game.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 509-513: for two finite isomorphic downward closed subsets S and T of the labelled tree of a structure, enumerated as (x_i) and (y_i), the tuple S stands in the rank alpha back-and-forth relation to T exactly when each x_i does to the corresponding y_i. The statement reduces a comparison of two sets to a coordinatewise comparison, and the proof (source lines 516-544) has to justify that reduction: it first moves the comparison to the upper cones of the points by observing that a formula about a cone is a formula about its root with all quantifiers restricted above it, then replaces those cones by the disjoint regions lying above exactly one enumeration point, which is legitimate only because the branches of the labelled tree are infinitely replicated, and finally argues by contradiction in the back-and-forth game, where the existential player answers inside each region separately and ends up with a winning strategy. The replication fact and the region partition are the substance of the argument and neither appears in the statement.
